name: The Record
best_for: investigative documentaries: closed communities and institutions, cover-ups, silence and pressure, court cases, rulings, how a system protects itself
look: The case assembled from the record itself. Blue-black ink ground with a faint ledger grid, bone-white paper pages, steel-grey labels and one sodium-amber signal for what matters (a marked line, the number that gives it away); a muted red only for stamps and verdicts. Statements in Crimson Pro, labels in condensed caps, files and courts in Kode Mono, Hebrew in Frank Ruhl Libre. Footage plays inside an evidence viewer (exhibit number, running timecode, source) - never as plain stock.

devices.use: Chapter heading: FILE 03 / 08, kicker, title, a docket line, the index of files lit at this one. One per act.
A ruling, statement or guidance as a line-numbered page; lines arrive as spoken (lineAt), [[key words]] get the amber marker (hiAt).
A term the story turns on: Hebrew word, transliteration, pronunciation, numbered meanings. On the word's first mention.
A ledger of numbers as bars that count up row by row (rows=[{label,value,at,hi,strikeAt}]); stamp on the verdict of the numbers.
A sentence board: two or three big counts and what happened after (strikeAt, after, stamp).
How the system works: nodes joined by arrows lighting on their words; a gate node, a delay clock, a block (x) on the last link.
A list whose names are blacked out one by one - names withheld, records sealed. Never shows a real private name.
Posters pasted on a night wall; the last carries one word, stamped (pashkevil / public shaming / notices).
A time axis (centuries or months): ticks, a marker that travels, events landing on their words.
A person at the centre with the rings of a life (school, job, marriage...); rings appear on their words and are cut away (cutAt).
A field of votes turning as one bloc - endorsements, block voting, a crowd that moves together.
Footage inside the evidence viewer (render clip inset=box): EXHIBIT number, running timecode, caption, source. Stock is always framed.
A citation tag on a picture: SOURCE - publication, year. Every figure or claim taken from a report.
Where we are: place name + a coordinates / date line, lower left.
Where it happens (dark map, amber pins).

rules: Every claim is part of the record: rulings and statements as transcript pages, figures as tally rows with their SOURCE, places with a place line. Nothing is written before the narrator says it (lineAt / hiAt / at on the word).
Footage is never plain stock: every clip plays inside the casebox viewer (exhibit number, timecode, caption) or carries a source tag; clips are under 5 s, chained when a line is longer.
No faces of victims or private people, no influencers / YouTubers / talking heads, no interviews; posters and lists never show a real private name.
About 30 % moving footage, 70 % photographs and graphics; a graphic at least every 40 s; one docket per act.
Calm motion: pages drift (<= 3.5 %), stamps land once, the marker sweeps once. Sound: paper, a typewriter tick for typed lines, a low hit for stamps, soft whooshes on headings - all under the voice.
